page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model, supported by 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.0 GB of memory per core. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics. Single-core processing is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the bottom 10% (779.18) and single-threaded bzip3 decompression rated as weak (7.69 GB/sec). However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 12409.56 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13359.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, averaging 48.36 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 28.85 GB/sec for write operations. Text processing stands out as a strength, scoring in the top 25% on Geekbench with 2638.0.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the contrast between weak single-core and average multi-core performance, this server is positioned for workloads that can parallelize tasks without requiring sustained, dedicated single-thread performance. It is suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, text processing, and static web serving, which achieved a throughput of 11.93 GB/sec. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or intensive real-time LLM text generation, where the medium 7B model achieved only 5.07 tokens/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model provides a high density of memory and cores at a lower resource tier, making it a viable option for budget-conscious, horizontally scaled deployments.
